stories.title: Bitcoin gives back its election rally as Wall Street's tech selloff deepens
stories.summary: Wednesday's post-election bounce reversed on Thursday. Chip and AI stocks fell hard and bitcoin fell with them, moving like a tech stock. Traders who had borrowed to bet on higher prices were forced out, which made the drop faster.
points: Bitcoin hit an intraday low of $75,568, and nearly $1.1B of leveraged bets were forcibly closed over 24 hours, per The Block.
Most of the losses hit bets on rising prices: CoinGlass data cited by crypto.news shows $954.38M of longs liquidated vs $127.30M of shorts.
Late Thursday, Motley Fool had bitcoin down 5.65% at $75,880.60 and ether down 7.80% at $2,233.79.
The Nasdaq closed down 5.52% and the S&P 500 down 4.36%, per JournalArta's market close report.
Crypto stocks fell hard: Coinbase and Strategy were down about 10% and Circle 12% in the afternoon, per 24/7 Wall St; CoinDesk shows closes of $136.68, $129.32 and $69.44.

stories.title: Binance hack fallout: US bank regulators check in, and frozen-fund recovery votes are weeks away
stories.summary: After the record theft from Binance, US bank regulators began asking banks about unusual activity, per Reuters reporting relayed by Cointelegraph. Binance is also asking the Arbitrum and Polygon communities to release stolen funds those networks froze.
points: About $6.34B was affected and $2.85B had been frozen or intercepted, per Binance's 3 Nov incident report as cited by Cointelegraph.
Fed and OCC officials began contacting US banks on Monday about unusual activity, per Cointelegraph, citing Reuters.
Binance asked Arbitrum's DAO to return 8,425.997 ETH and 74.56M ARB; it expects the process to take seven weeks or longer, per crypto.news.
A Polygon proposal would move about 70.49M POL to recovery wallets (46.63M linked to Binance, 23.86M to Polymarket), valued at about $6.5M by The Merkle.
Polygon's governance call took it up on 5 Nov; no outcome had been reported when this page was updated. If approved, The Merkle says rollout would take about two weeks.

stories.title: Democrats' Congress stalls the crypto market-structure bill
stories.summary: After Democrats' sweeping midterm wins, analysts say passing the CLARITY Act has become tougher. House Democrats are discussing their own bill that would give the SEC more power over crypto markets.
points: Stifel's Brian Gardner said the CLARITY Act is off the table for the lame-duck session and expects investigations of crypto firms, per 24/7 Wall St.
House Democrats are discussing expanding Rep. Maxine Waters' Crypto Investor Consumer Bill of Rights into a broader market-structure bill, with more power for the SEC, per Decrypt.
GSR's Carlos Guzman told Decrypt it is not game over for CLARITY, but passing it has become tougher.
